relevance_note: Case report of a Palestinian family with Blau syndrome in which 'the proband and all three family members had an R334q mutation in the CARD15/Nod2 gene', with individual-level detail for the proband, her sister and her father.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; no table in the paper; output assembled with a short Python script from hand-written values and every span checked verbatim against the Markdown. Three in-scope people are described: the proband (label 'patient', rule 5: single unnamed index patient of this case report; role words not used), her sister ('sister of patient') and their father ('father of patient'). The abstract says 'the proband and all three family members had an R334q mutation'; it is unclear whether 'three family members' includes the proband or a further relative (the pedigree in Fig. 2 is an image not available as text, and the mother is never described), so no row was created for any other relative and n_patients_reported is left null. Variant rows for sister and father rest on that abstract sentence; their zygosity and 'missense' type come from the group sentence 'genetic analysis for the patient and her family ... revealed a heterozygous gain-of-function missense mutation', applied as a statement about the named group 'the patient and her family'. Inheritance for the proband left 'not reported': the paper never states explicitly that the father carries the variant by naming him; 'all three family members' is not a named-parent statement. Bronchiectasis is recorded as observed; the authors' remark that it 'could be as a result of an underlying interstitial lung disease' is hedged, so the interstitial lung disease checklist item is not reported. Normal complete blood count, kidney and liver function tests were recorded as written (a general normal investigation), not as exclusions of more specific checklist items (renal failure, hepatic involvement remain not reported). Blurred vision was recorded as a feature but the checklist item 'visual impairment or blindness' was left not reported. Skin rash checklist item marked excluded from 'Our patient had no history of skin involvement' although the authors add the diagnosis may have been missed. Ages for the sister (19 years) taken as age at last evaluation; the proband's age at diagnosis of BS (18) is given only for her. No contradictions found in the paper.
